reasoning_content:
We can use consistency YES/NO as prediction agreement?

The previously proposed use of consistency YES/NO as the prediction agreement is invalid. It is only a derived agreement, cannot serve as both a clinical outcome and assay prediction indicator, lacks a universal applicable threshold for IC50 scoring, and does not carry sufficient predictive information by itself.

Multiple attempts to find a valid solution have been made, but all proposed schemes either rely on unvalidated thresholds or fail to meet the requirements of independent identifiable assay and outcome evidence. Only aggregate count data is available, which cannot meet the schema requirements, so reconstruction is likely blocked.

Target’s demand for a headline has brought new twists to the issue. Existing rules explicitly prohibit using only consistency flags to meet assay or outcome evidence requirements, and a threshold-free accuracy evaluation is not feasible. I will search relevant literature for regimen-specific IC50 threshold standards.
